content.title: Project Setup
bullets:
Create a new Flutter project:
				`flutter create my_app`
Open the project in your IDE.
Overview of the project structure:
lib/main.dart (main entry point)
pubspec.yaml (dependencies and assets)
android/, ios/, web/, test/ folders.

content.title: Understanding main.dart
bullets: In Flutter, the main() function is the entry point of the application—just like in any Dart program. It is where the execution of the app begins.
Every Flutter app must have a main() function.
It is automatically called when the app starts.
Inside main(), you usually call runApp() with the root widget of your application.
runApp() attaches the given widget to the screen and makes it the root of the widget tree.
StatelessWidget: Immutable (cannot change after being built).
StatelessWidget: Used when the UI does not need to update dynamically.
Example: A static text label, an icon, or a fixed image.
StatefulWidget : Mutable (can change dynamically).
Used when the UI needs to update (e.g., counters, forms, animations).
Example: A button that changes color when pressed, a counter app.
